title: Stress-Testing Targeted-Instruction-Pair Deception Probes Across Datasets

original_idea.body:
# Stress-Testing Targeted-Instruction-Pair Deception Probes Across Datasets

**Problem:** Building Better Deception Probes Using Targeted Instruction Pairs (arXiv:2602.01425, Feb 2026) builds stronger deception probes, but related work notes deception is heterogeneous: probes that work on one deception dataset may fail on another (e.g. sandbagging responds best to concealment-focused prompts).

**Direction:** Reimplement the targeted-instruction-pair probe construction on an open model, then evaluate cross-dataset transfer: train on one deception dataset (e.g. roleplay lying) and test on a different one (e.g. sandbagging). Produce a transfer matrix quantifying how much detectability degrades across deception types.

**Why it matters:** Honest measurement of how brittle deception probes are across deception subtypes is essential before anyone trusts them for oversight, and it requires only open models and small labeled datasets.

**Relevant context:** Building Better Deception Probes Using Targeted Instruction Pairs (arXiv:2602.01425, Feb 2026); deception heterogeneity noted in deception-probe literature (sandbagging responds best to concealment-focused prompts).
